Policy.description: How a worker admits one offloaded unit: a machine offers itself (headroom) when its smallest unit fits (`smallestMegabytes`), the free memory it reports is what a unit may still take above its floor, and a unit is admitted when its own predicted peak fits into that beside the part of their peaks the running units have not grown into yet. Raised memory pressure (`warn`) alone refuses only units above `warnMaximumMegabytes` and every unit while swap is growing; critical pressure refuses all. How many units a machine lends while its readiness stage runs is decided by measured memory alone (the stage keeps its own reserve through its claim): a fixed count of one unit per stage left every worker whose stage read for hours unable to take a component final although it had the memory. CPU counts too: a machine whose one-minute load average per core is at or above `loadPerCoreCeilingPermille` (thousandths of a load per core) refuses with `load` and reports no headroom, so a saturated machine is never offered work. The coordinator (an origin ending in `coordinatorOriginSuffix`, the group server) keeps `coordinatorReservedSlots` of its slots for its own interactive work: it registers that many fewer.

Messages.description: The sentences of the CPU refusal, English and German: `load` is the one-minute load average of the machine, `cores` its core count and `ceiling` the declared load per core (`Policy.loadPerCoreCeilingPermille`) as a decimal.

en.load: load {load} on {cores} cores is at or above the ceiling of {ceiling} per core: the machine is busy with its own work

de.load: Last {load} auf {cores} Kernen liegt auf oder über der Obergrenze von {ceiling} pro Kern: die Maschine ist mit eigener Arbeit ausgelastet
